definitions.explanation: A size that can be eaten in a single bite. Very common in cooking instructions and recipes.

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}を{一口大|ひとくちだい}に{切|き}る。
examples.english: Cut the vegetables into bite-sized pieces.

examples.japanese: {鶏肉|とりにく}は{一口大|ひとくちだい}にして{下味|したあじ}を{付|つ}ける。
examples.english: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and season it.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{食|た}べやすいように、{一口大|ひとくちだい}に{切|き}ってあげた。
examples.english: I cut it into bite-sized pieces so that the child could eat easily.

notes:
USAGE:
{一口大|ひとくちだい} is one of the most common instructions in Japanese recipes. It describes cutting food into pieces small enough to eat in one bite. The suffix {大|だい} here means "size."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一口大|ひとくちだい}に{切|き}る (to cut into bite-sized pieces)
- {一口大|ひとくちだい}にする (to make bite-sized)
- {一口大|ひとくちだい}にちぎる (to tear into bite-sized pieces)

GRAMMAR:
Used as a noun that modifies with に: 〜を{一口大|ひとくちだい}に{切|き}る. The {大|だい} suffix meaning "size" also appears in words like {手|て}のひら{大|だい} (palm-sized).
